correctness.rationale: For a full-dimensional centrally symmetric polytope Q, (B+λQ)\(S+λQ) is exactly {x: x−λQ lies inside the open unit ball}, since x−λQ is convex and intersects the ball. Symmetric farthest vertices force λ²R²+||x||²+2λh_P(Π_W x)<1, so it vanishes exactly at λR=1. Nonfarthest vertices are inactive near this threshold because their squared norm has a positive finite gap. Writing δ=1−λ²R², x_W=δy and x_perp=√δ z yields exponent s+(d−s)/2=(d+s)/2; integration over z gives C=(R/2)^s vol(P°) π^((d−s)/2) Γ(s+1)/Γ(s+1+(d−s)/2) with O(δ) relative error by uniform sublevel bracketing. The rhombus shield condition √(1−λ²a²)+λb≤1 is equivalent to λ≥2b/(a²+b²). At a>b, coefficient 4/3 and exponent 3/2; at a=b, coefficient 1 and exponent 2. I independently evaluated direct four-disk quadrant intersections at a=2,b=1, λ=.2,.4,.45,.49: below .4 true area is smaller than two-disk lens (1.52775924<1.58534685 at .2), at and above .4 exact lens agreement; a=b examples also distinguished the symmetry boundary.
